questions.q: Who did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to prophesy against?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to prophesy against the people of Ammon.

questions.q: What did the people of Ammon do when the sanctuary was profaned and the house of Judah went into exile?
questions.a: When the sanctuary was profaned and the house of Judah went into exile, the people of Ammon said, “Aha!”

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to the people of Ammon because of what they said when the house of Judah went into exile?
questions.a: Yahweh will give the people of Ammon to a people in the east.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to Ammon that will cause them to know that Yahweh is Lord?
questions.a: Yahweh will cut Ammon off from the other peoples and destroy them.

questions.q: What did Moab and Seir say when the house of Judah went into exile?
questions.a: When the house of Judah went into exile, Moab and Seir said that the house of Judah was like every other nation.

questions.q: What will no longer be remembered among the nations?
questions.a: The people of Ammon will no longer be remembered among the nations.

questions.q: What had Edom done against the house of Judah?
questions.a: Edom had exacted vengeance against the house of Judah.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to Edom because of what Edom did to the house of Judah?
questions.a: Yahweh will destroy every person and animal in Edom.

questions.q: What had the Philistines done against the house of Judah?
questions.a: The Philistines had taken vengeance with disdain against the house of Judah.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to the Philistines because of what the Philistines did to the house of Judah?

commentary.text: Judgments against the Ammonites. (Ezek. 25:1-7) Against the Moabites, Edomites, and Philistines. (Ezek. 25:8-17)

Ezek. 25:1-7. It is wicked to be glad at the calamities of any, especially of God's people; it is a sin for which he will surely reckon. God will make it appear that he is the God of Israel, though he suffers them for a time to be captives in Babylon. It is better to know Him, and to be poor, than to be rich and ignorant of him.

Ezek. 25:8-17 Though one event seem to the righteous and wicked, it is vastly different. Those who glory in any other defence and protection than the Divine power, providence, and promise, will, sooner or later, be ashamed of their glorying. Those who will not leave it to God to take vengeance for them, may expect that he will take vengeance on them. The equity of the Lord's judgments is to be observed, when he not only avenges injuries upon those that did them, but by those against whom they were done. Those who treasure up old hatred, and watch for the opportunity of manifesting it, are treasuring up for themselves wrath against the day of wrath.
